The sweet soy sauce goes well with the tuna in the tuna braised in soy sauce, and the fried aralia shrimp rolls have a slightly sour taste.

The tuna belly is very oily and soft, and the scallops are soft as if they have been aged.
Smoked yellowtail straw has a smoky flavor that may be unfamiliar, and the yellowtail fin meat is chewy like squid and really delicious.
Anago has a rat-like scent but is surprisingly good, and Ume Shiso Maki's cucumber cleanses the palate.

People may have different opinions on Shari, but since she is a bit sticky, I think each person will feel it differently.
The rice does not seem to be of the highest quality and has a rough feeling in the mouth.
I think it would have been better if the amount of rice had been increased to make me full.

At this price, it is a really good sushi restaurant in a location called Yeoksam.
However, the salty liver and small amount are disappointing.
The price-quality ratio is high, but if you want to eat to your fill, you may want to consider other places.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

reviews.author: kaku hayashi
reviews.text:
Level 2 spiciness for basic kakuni and boiled chicken
What should I say about this taste?
I don't think it can be compared to the taste I had in Sapporo, Japan. It's similar, but you can't find the deep flavor.
To express the local texture and taste of Japan, the chicken is so soft that you can bone it with just a fork, and the soup is so rich and spicy that you want to eat it all the way to the end. Even though various vegetables are grilled and fried, their texture remains intact. In fact, the vegetable part was disappointing, and the texture of the chicken legs in particular made me wonder if I should tear them apart. The rice doesn't seem to be Koshihikari. It has a sticky texture, so you should have the rich taste of carbohydrates when eating it with soup, but this part is also somewhat disappointing.
If I were to visit, I think stage 3 would have been better. Level 2 seems to have almost no spiciness.
Since it is a personal preference, there will definitely be differences from person to person, but revisiting it is a concern. I don't know if the food tastes different at each store, but I think it's a management issue that the quality should be the same no matter which store you go to.
Being constantly compared to the local area may be a problem in itself.
However. The opening of a soup curry restaurant in Gangnam is an opportunity, and I think it's definitely a good thing. The highball was really good because it was proportioned well. Looks like you have skill ^^

reviews.author: Jueon
reviews.text:
Gangnam Restaurant Katsu Workshop Gangnam Branch is located between Gangnam Station and Shinnonhyeon Station!

The store is located in the middle of Gangnam's core commercial district, making it easy to access and convenient for making appointments or stopping by for lunch.

In particular, the area between Gangnam Station and Shinnonhyeon Station has a very large floating population, so even first-time visitors can easily find it.
Since it is slightly inside rather than a noisy place on the main street, it has a good atmosphere for concentrating on your meal.

Accessibility to public transportation is accessible from both Gangnam Station and Shinnonhyeon Station.
Visitors using Line 9 or Shinbundang Line can walk from Shinnonhyeon Station, and visitors using Line 2 can walk from Gangnam Station.

Also, if you come by bus, you can use the bus stops around Gangnam-daero.
It can be said that there is a wide range of transportation options.

The area around the store is full of offices, schools, shopping, cafes, movie theaters, bars, and restaurants.
It can be fully used as a lunch place for office workers, a place to eat before an appointment, a place to eat before/after watching a movie, or a place to eat alone.

The exterior of the Katsu Workshop Gangnam branch is located in an alley between Gangnam Station and Shinnonhyeon Station.
It stands out for its sophisticated minimalist style without being overly flashy.

The store sign is written in black with the company name "Katsu Workshop" clearly engraved on it.
It was written in a modern font so it was easy to recognize even from a distance.

The entire store is made up of wide glass windows, allowing the interior light to gently seep in.
During the day, natural light is reflected, creating a bright and refreshing atmosphere, and at night, warm lights illuminate the alley, creating a cozy atmosphere.

Photos of the store's various menus are posted below the store windows and next to the entrance.
It's a good idea to check the menu at least once before visiting the store or when passing by.

The store entrance is decorated in a clean and casual atmosphere reminiscent of a Japanese restaurant.

It is decorated in white and wood tones, giving a warm and cozy impression.
Small lights on both sides of the entrance give it a more luxurious feel.

As the store is located in the Gangnam commercial district, it maintains a sophisticated atmosphere but is not overly simple.
It has an interior where you can enjoy everything from eating alone to small gatherings without burden.

The overall tone is bright and clean, with white tones, wood tones, and soft lighting.
Warmth and coziness are added to create a comfortable dining atmosphere.

The tables are arranged efficiently with a focus on tables for 2 and 4.
The tables were spaced appropriately and there was a partition, so eye contact or conversation with the guests next to me was not interrupted.

Also, there are no single tables or bar tables for solo guests, but the tables are compact in size so it doesn't feel awkward to sit alone.

On the wall of the store, there is a menu poster and a simple information board for the Katsu Workshop Gangnam branch.
A soft pendant light illuminates each table, maintaining good brightness for taking photos of food.

As a tonkatsu specialty restaurant, tonkatsu is the main menu, and the basic set includes rice and miso soup.
You can have a hearty meal without having to order anything extra.

The price range is in the low to mid-10,000 won per person range, making it a perfect lineup for office workers' lunch or light dinner.
Considering the freshness of the ingredients and the quality of the handmade tonkatsu, this is quite acceptable.

A basic tonkatsu set starts at around 13,000 won to 15,000 won.
The tonkatsu is thick and the deep-fried batter is excellent, making it more satisfying than the price.

reviews.author: JIYOO KIM

Enjoy it as ochazuke with broth, try it with just green onions, seaweed, and wasabi, or just enjoy it with plain rice and eel!!

reviews.text:
Went for dinner. The interior had a modern and clean atmosphere and the selection of dishes was good. Some of the food was good and some of it was disappointing. There are some food photos I wasn't able to take.

The sushi neta was generally okay, but the shari was very salty. Still, you can feel the balanced taste of oily fish such as herring, striped horse mackerel, and tuna belly when you chew them. However, it feels like it drowns out the taste of some netas such as sea bream fry, sweet shrimp, and tuna flesh.

The most memorable menu items from Tsumami are as follows.
Tuna meat wrapped in prosciutto, egg yolk and truffle sauce: it was full of flavor.
Seasoned freshwater eel fries: The taste is strong and junky, and I think I would have gotten sick of it if it weren't for the sour cucumber that came with it.
Tapas made with anquimo and shrimp heads: The taste of anquimo was overwhelmingly strong, so I couldn't really smell the shrimp heads. It was a bit difficult to eat in one bite.
Grilled cutlassfish: The small bones were removed so it was easy to eat. Instead of the mild seasoning, it was served with minced garlic and radish. Still, I wish it had a little more salt.
Steamed abalone: ​​It was the most delicious of all tsumami. The offal sauce was perfect, and the salty shari went really well when mixed with the remaining sauce.

reviews.author: korean
reviews.text:
🕒 When to visit
I visited during lunch time (between 12:20 and 30 p.m.), and luckily I was able to get in right away without waiting. But right after that, there was a wait.

🍽️Food
I ate Kyokai udon and karaage, and the aroma of seafood was clearly felt in the udon at the end, which was impressive. I chose the salty option, but it was less salty than what Japanese ramen restaurants usually add, so I think it would be good for Korean tastes. The karaage was delicious, faithful to the basics, and it was fun to eat with a variety of side dishes such as vinegared ginger and chives. Especially when I ate the chives and rice in the soup, I felt like I was at a soup restaurant.

🧑‍🍳Service
It was really heart-warming to see the grandmother personally tie an apron for us and treat us as “precious people.” It was a small act of kindness, but it was a heart-melting moment for the customer. This atmosphere made me want to make it my regular place.

🏠 Atmosphere
For a ramen restaurant, the interior was quite large. There were most bar tables, and there were several tables that could seat 4 people. However, since it is located inside the building, it can be a bit lost when you first find it.

🚗 Other Tips
During lunch hours, there is a waiting list quickly, so I recommend visiting a little before 12 o'clock. There are a variety of side dishes and side dishes, so we recommend trying the soup-and-rice dish.

🔁 Willingness to visit again
The taste is satisfying, and most of all, the friendly service makes this a place I want to visit again. It was a good enough place to be a regular. Grandma is so sweet

reviews.author: When will I go on a diet?
reviews.text:
While I was in Gangnam, I went to Kinka, number 1, and after digesting my food, I came to Wasshoi Ken, number 2.
People who visited said they tried Gyodon Gyodon, so I followed the trend and ordered Kyokai Tonkotsu! (Egg chashu added, Japanese saltiness)

First of all, when I tried the soup, the smell of fish and shellfish led at the beginning, followed by the pork from the middle to the finish.
I thought it was a good decision to choose Japanese liver because the taste was quite intuitive and had a lot of umami.

The noodles were not completely hard, but had a moderate texture and were thin, so of course they went well with tonkotsu.

However, the toppings were very disappointing.
The pork belly is thin and oily, and the mushroom taste is familiar.
I especially didn't like the ham-like chashu. It had a peculiar spice-like smell... hmm, not to my taste!

Other than that, I was surprised to see rice, chives, and kimchi in the self-service corner.
A big advantage is that there are two Korean side dishes that can be refreshed at a ramen restaurant.

In summary, the layers of fish and pork were clearly felt in the soup, and the balance was good.
However, the toppings were a bit disappointing, but the side dishes at the self-serve corner soothed my disappointment.
If I go near Gangnam Station again, I want to visit again. It was a good meal😀

The quality can be said to be higher in Oreno, but personally, this one suits my taste better. (For reference, the taste was good, but I don't like the original Japanese style, so Oreno is also 4 stars here)

reviews.author: WOONG’s KITCHEN
reviews.text:
Mennoah. Even though it wasn't grilled, I boarded the bus toward Gangnam Station with excitement, thinking about the tripe I would meet after a long time.

When I entered the restaurant, there were some people waiting, but looking at the atmosphere, it seemed like one person would get a seat quickly. (Nice) So I immediately ordered beef tripe ramen (level 1, spiciness adjustable) and chicken skin gyoza through the kiosk.

The ramen was quickly served, and I was surprised to see that there was more crispy grilled giblets than I expected, which was nice. When I tasted the soup, it wasn't thick and spicy, and the tripe didn't seem to be involved in the broth. The generous amount of tripe was mostly full and had a rich taste and aroma. Tripe ramen made by tripe, for tripe.

Because they added plenty of green onions and minced garlic out of concern about the greasiness, the spicy taste reminded me of tripe casserole. It was delicious, but the more I ate it, the more Korean it became, which made me think about the definition of ramen.

The chicken skin gyoza I ordered as a side was also nice. The gyoza, which was filled with soft and fatty ground meat inside a thin and chewy chicken skin, had a good combination of meat flavor and ginger flavor. It comes in four small pieces, and it tastes like I will definitely order it again next time.

Personally, I wondered if I could put beef tripe ramen in the ramen category, but it was clear that it was a delicious bowl of food with good value for money. And the employees, the store atmosphere, and the customers all had an energetic and pleasant feeling. It was a meaningful time in many ways. My intention to revisit is yes.

reviews.author: CHANGHWAN YOO (Independent traveler)
reviews.text:
A Chinese restaurant with really delicious sweet and sour pork.
If you want to visit here for lunch, you might want to hurry. This is because the wait may be long due to the influx of office workers during their lunch hour. There are two menus for jjamppong rice, basic and samseon, and as the seafood differs greatly, the price also differs by 5,000 won. Even with basic jjamppong rice, you can enjoy the clean, refreshing taste of the spicy soup. Ganjjajang is mixed well with the heavy and rich jjajang sauce and the plump noodles, so you can feel the intense taste of jjajang. However, as you eat it, the jjajang sauce can feel very salty, so you can enjoy it by adding a bowl of rice. The sweet and sour pork was one of the most delicious sweet and sour pork I've had in Gangnam. The thick meat inside the soft and crispy batter was chewed gently while retaining plenty of juice. The taste of the meat may be masked by the strong sauce, but the sauce here is neither too strong nor too weak, and helps to enhance the flavor of the fried meat. Although it is quite a bit more expensive than regular sweet and sour pork, I enjoyed it so much that I don't think it was a choice I would regret.

reviews.author: Roxie Kang
reviews.text:
A Chinese restaurant that never fails.

I went to Chungkyung Maratang for company dinners and lunches, and was so satisfied that I took my family with me!

There are many types of Chinese food, close to local tastes.
I ordered Mara Xianggu as the default and added whatever I wanted. (I haven’t tried Malatang)

In Gangnam, Malatang has become so popular since the year before last that there are many competing companies, but the taste is so good that they even opened a second branch here, and the service is not bad. The store is spacious, the hygiene is good, and it seems like a lot of office workers come here to eat malatang or rice bowls during lunch time.

My personal tip is... eggplant is really delicious in Chinese cuisine, so if you order eggplant dish, it's usually a success. (I was originally a picky eater in Korea.)

✔️The first photo is Mara Xiangguo, who everyone is familiar with. it's good. Personally, I like lamb, enoki mushrooms, and meatballs.

☝️For Chinese food, you can guess the cooking method or ingredients by looking at the name.
✔️The food in the middle shown in the second photo is a food called ‘Gyeongjangyukseul’. Gyeongjang is a slightly salty sauce similar to chunjang, and yukseul is thin, long slices of meat.
It tastes like wrapping cold tofu skin with various vegetables such as meat and cucumbers and sauces, and it is refreshingly delicious. (Sweet, salty, sweet and salty) It's the taste of various ingredients subtly mixing in your mouth.
✔️On the left is a food called Jisamseon, which means three fresh ingredients from the ground and is usually made by frying and stir-frying potatoes, bell peppers, and eggplant. (sweet salty sweet salty) I ate a lot when I was in China👍
✔️The one on the right is Kkoobarou. Like Korean sweet and sour pork.. This is a food that most people in Korea know. It's soft, the sauce is sweet, and it's really delicious.

Other than that, it's not in the picture, but when I went with my family, I also tried cream shrimp, stir-fried tomato eggs, and peeled squid, and everyone enjoyed them.
Chinese food not only includes spicy foods like malatang/xiangguo, but also has a variety of foods depending on the region, so it would be a good idea to try it.

A place with reasonable prices, hygiene, and taste all in one!

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I tried to go on the weekend several times, but couldn't because they said it was closed on Sundays and 3 o'clock on Saturdays, but this time I made up my mind and decided to visit.

First, the sweet and sour pork, which I was most looking forward to, had a slightly black sauce because it contained Chinese soy sauce, and the taste of the sauce was more sour than sweet as you can see. Carrots and onions, which are often seen in sweet and sour pork sauce, are also sliced ​​and apples are different from other places. The fried meat has just the right amount of meat, the batter is chewy due to the glutinous rice in it, and the smell is not perfect, but it's good.

The noodles of handmade jjajangmyeon are thin and wide like kalguksu (noodles) rather than round. The color of the Jjajang sauce is a bit light, but the seasoning is a bit strong, and as the name of this restaurant suggests, it has the overall feel of old-fashioned Jjajangmyeon. It seems like the sauce was made with shortening, so it was a bit greasy, so I wasn't very impressed.

Lastly, the fried rice had a common shortening flavor and was nothing special. The jjamppong soup that came with it was salty.

Pickled radish, onion, and chachai are served on the side, and the chachai is very seasoned.

In conclusion, it's worth stopping by if you're looking for sweet and sour pork when you're nearby, but if you're thinking of Jjajangmyeon or fried rice, it might not be great overall... It's not something you'd come across as a restaurant better than a local Chinese restaurant.

The foreign country near Seoul National University that I visited recently was better than here.

No intention to revisit.
